title: Collect client review comments | Verse Engine by Ctruh
description: Collect client review comments in the Verse Engine by Ctruh docs: what it is, how to use it, and where it fits in your 3D workflow.

docs.article:
Collect client review comments#

A share link doubles as a review round. Your client opens it, clicks any spot in the scene and types a note; the comment is pinned to that exact 3D position and everyone who opens the link sees the numbered pin. You, as the owner, resolve or delete pins and watch the open count fall. No client account is needed.

You need: a published scene. To moderate, you need to own it (see Share privately with tokens for creating an account and claiming a scene). Every call below was run against a live server.

1. Send the link#

Any share link works: https://HOST/?vpk=ingest/<id>.vpk. For a private scene, send a per-reviewer tokened link (…&share=<shareToken>) — comments are gated exactly like the scene bytes, so a stranger without the token gets a 404 from the review routes too.

2. What the reviewer does#

  1. Once the scene is up, a Review chip appears. They toggle it on.
  2. They click a surface — orbit or walk mode alike (the pick is GPU-side, so it works on streamed scenes of any size) — and a small composer opens at that spot.
  3. They type the note (up to 500 characters), optionally their name, and post. A numbered pin appears, projected from world to screen and faded with distance.

Existing pins open on click to show the note. Pins are capped at 200 per scene; posting is rate-limited to 60 per hour per IP.

3. What you see#

Open the same link signed in (the /studio session cookie, or the token pasted into the playground) and every pin gains Resolve and Delete. Resolved pins grey out and hide behind a show resolved toggle. Your /studio scene cards show open / total per scene, as does GET /v1/account/scenes (reviews: { open, total }).

The same thing over HTTP#

Useful for a review dashboard of your own, or to pull comments into an issue tracker.

Post a comment (anonymous; author optional):

Code
curl -sS -X POST "https://HOST/v1/review/docs-demo-718035483f84" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"pos":[1.2,0.9,-0.4],"text":"Can we see this wall in the oak finish?","author":"Priya"}'
# → {"id":"c76ae3e41a","t":1790833830642}

Read them all (oldest first, resolved ones included):

Code
curl -sS "https://HOST/v1/review/docs-demo-718035483f84"
# → {"scene":"docs-demo-718035483f84","comments":[
#      {"id":"c76ae3e41a","t":1790833830642,"pos":[1.2,0.9,-0.4],
#       "text":"Can we see this wall in the oak finish?","author":"Priya","resolved":false}]}

On a private scene add ?share=<shareToken> (or X-Verse-Share: <shareToken>) to both calls.

Moderate as the owner:

Code
curl -sS -X POST "https://HOST/v1/review/docs-demo-718035483f84/c76ae3e41a/resolve" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer TOKEN"
# → {"id":"c76ae3e41a","resolved":true}

curl -sS -X DELETE "https://HOST/v1/review/docs-demo-718035483f84/c76ae3e41a" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer TOKEN"
# → {"deleted":"c76ae3e41a"}

Errors follow the error contract: 400 bad shape, 404 no such scene (or private without access — existence is never advertised), 413 text over 500 characters or the scene at 200 comments, 429 rate limited, 401 moderation without account auth.

In an embed on your own site#

Pass review: true and wire your own toggle; the composer renders inside the iframe, fits embeds down to 320 px wide, and fires events you can mirror into a sidebar:

Code
const viewer = Verse.embed(el, { scene: "docs-demo-718035483f84", review: true });
toggle.onchange = () => viewer.setReviewMode(toggle.checked);
viewer.on("review-posted",   (d) => addToSidebar(d));          // { id, pos, text }
viewer.on("review-selected", (d) => highlightInSidebar(d.id));
const all = await viewer.getComments();                         // same shape as GET /v1/review/<id>

Owner moderation stays in the playground and /studio by design — an embed viewer, even the owner, only ever sees the anonymous composer. Full option list: Embed SDK reference.

Where comments live#

A per-scene append-only JSONL under the dotfile directory ingest/.reviews/ on the server — never served, skipped by the sweeper, deleted with the scene (owner delete or disk-budget eviction).
